function.mechanism: Azo chromophore absorbs visible light and imparts yellow color to foods and supplements.

adi.basis: EFSA ANS re-evaluation (2009) maintained ADI; no reason to revise from previous value.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA re-evaluation concluded no reason to revise ADI of 7.5 mg/kg bw/day; impurity exposure under current specifications was not considered a safety concern.

adi.basis: JECFA (2016) established ADI range 0-10 mg/kg bw from NOAEL 984 mg/kg bw/day with UF 100; withdrew previous 0-7.5 mg/kg bw/day ADI.

concerns.summary: Regulatory labeling in U.S. drug context warns FD&C Yellow No. 5 may cause allergic-type reactions including bronchial asthma in susceptible persons, especially with aspirin hypersensitivity.

Human challenge-trial and review literature report associations between synthetic food dye exposure and behavioral effects in some children; several recent animal studies report cognitive/behavioral changes under chronic exposure models.
Recent integrated OECD/AOP-oriented analysis suggests potential endocrine activity signals primarily from in silico/in vitro integration, requiring confirmation in robust in vivo/human datasets.
Multiple recent rodent/zebrafish studies report oxidative stress and organ-level changes under experimental exposures; translational relevance to normal dietary intake remains uncertain.

no_concern_confirmed: No positive IARC carcinogenic group classification was identified in the current IARC classification dataset accessed.
JECFA 2016 concluded estimated dietary exposure, including children 1-10 years, was below the upper ADI bound.

adi_exceedance.notes: JECFA 2016 reported population exposure estimates below upper ADI; however, susceptible subgroups (e.g., behaviorally sensitive children, dye-sensitive individuals) remain a practical concern independent of simple ADI exceedance.

risk_assessment.rationale: Tartrazine is approved by EFSA/FDA/JECFA with explicit ADIs and regulatory controls, but evidence base includes persistent caveats: behavioral signals in children for synthetic dye exposures, repeated animal toxicity findings, and hypersensitivity warnings. This supports a moderate, not high, risk tier under current evidence.
key_factors: Approved in major jurisdictions with ADI
Behavioral concern signals in pediatric literature
No confirmed current IARC carcinogenic group listing
